text:
jamie (support): Heads-up — customer `acme-ai` on hosted inference reporting intermittent 502s and long request hangs since ~09:42 UTC. They see a heap of gateway 502s but traces show TLS handshake timeouts for a subset of requests. Putting the short repro + logs below.

ash_oncall: ACK. Can you paste the minimal repro and any DNS/traceroute/dig output? Also was anything deployed to edge in last hour?

jamie (support): Repro we used from their environment (they're on eu-west):
```
curl -v "https://inference-host.redwood.example/v1/generate" -H "Host: acme.example" --max-time 10
*   Trying 2001:db8:abcd::1:443...\n* TCP_NODELAY set\n* Connection timed out during TLS handshake\n* Closing connection 0\n* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, handshake failure (some)
curl: (35) error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
```
We also ran openssl against the edge IP from the same client network:
```
openssl s_client -connect 2001:db8:abcd::1:443 -servername acme.example -timeout 5
CONNECTED(00000003)
140735...: SSL handshake timeout
---
no peer certificate
---
```
And dig from the same host: 
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> acme.example @8.8.8.8
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1, AUTH: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; OPT PSEUDOSECTION:
; EDNS: version: 0, flags:; udp: 512, DO: false
;; WARNING: recursion requested but not available
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;acme.example. IN A
;; ANSWER SECTION:
acme.example.  60 IN A  203.0.113.55
;; Query time: 45 msec
```
Then a repeat query (same network) returned with TC=1 and the resolver fell back to TCP, which was much slower and correlated with the fraction of requests hitting the broken path.

li_eng_runtime: Interesting — TC bit then TCP fallback could explain extra RTTs, but not handshake timeouts on TLS unless something is mangling the TCP payload (SNI get stripped) or a middlebox is interfering. Any evidence of partial cert chain changes or cert rotation?

support-bot: cert-rotation-event: edge-cert-rotation completed at 3951234400 (recent intermediate push to CDN vendors).

jamie (support): We saw the cert chain differ when fetching the cert from some edge nodes vs others — some nodes served full chain, others served only leaf. Customer traced failing flows to IPv6 path (their traffic prefers IPv6). IPv4 path mostly OK.

priya_cs: Customer says impact is ~5% of their requests (a mix of model sizes). They asked if we can route them away from affected edge nodes while we investigate.

ash_oncall: Actions: 1) Can eng-runtime run an immediate small-scale drain+restart of the targeted edge TCP proxy pool to evict any bad upstream TCP proxies? 2) Can we confirm which DNS vendor/EDNS0 behaviour is returning TC to their resolver? 3) Ask customer for a pcap of the failed handshake if possible (capture the ClientHello/ServerHello exchange).

li_eng_runtime: On it — I'll kick off a rolling restart of the eu-west tcp-proxy pool (low-risk canary first). Also will add a quick probe that performs an openssl s_client —servername check over both v4 and v6 to detect SNI/chain inconsistencies across nodes.

jamie (support): For the customer workaround we suggested: force IPv4 for the host in their environment (use `--resolve` or set an A-only DNS), or pin to another region temporarily. They confirmed IPv4 resolves the failures.

priya_cs: Customer appreciated a workaround but asked for permanent fix. Can we surface ETA?

li_eng_runtime: Need to confirm root cause after probes. Hypothesis: edge cert rotation + a subset of upstream TCP proxies (or CDN partners) are incorrectly truncating or failing to forward the full TLS handshake when connections fall back to TCP after EDNS0/UDP truncation. If probes confirm SNI or cert chain loss on some nodes we'll roll back to known-good cert bundle and coordinate with CDN partner to ensure correct chain delivery.

jamie (support): I've asked customer for a pcap and sample client IPs. Also asked for the exact resolver they use (they're on a corporate resolver that proxies to FastName DNS).

ash_oncall: Thanks. Next steps: eng-runtime to confirm via probes (li), restart pool (li), support to collect pcap + client IPs (jamie), CS to communicate mitigation and keep customer updated (priya). I'll follow up in 30m. :eyes:

li_eng_runtime: Starting canary restart now and running cross-node openssl probes. Will report results here. :white_check_mark:

jamie (support): thx — will paste anything new from the customer here when I get it. :thumbsup:
